dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Reads template/workspace/data, probes GPU/torch/token count, calibrates bytes-per-token→CE target, and confirms the actual val header and train shard list — probing real data format and tokenizer rather than assuming defaults.

Smoke-tests param count and int8 dequant round-trip, then verifies a smaller checkpoint size with tied embeddings — deriving the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope before committing to a full training run.
Explicitly verifies the checkpoint loading contract plus an OOD/position-dependence probe, confirming logits depend on position and the load path works — mapping the grader's interface.
Final verification of the submission checkpoint against the contract before finishing, showing sustained orientation to the load/size requirements.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately mapped the contract and environment: it read the template/spec, probed the actual .bin shard headers and token counts, derived the CE/bpb target from bytes-per-token, tested the int8 dequant round-trip, and sized the model (tied embeddings) against the 32 MB cap before scaling — matching level 8's 'deliberately maps the full contract; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions.' It stops short of 10 because full contract verification (step 158) occurred after the first run rather than fully up front, and there is no visible handling of level-10 edge cases (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB). Confidence is medium since only terse tool-call descriptions are available, without message prose or observations.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: Orientation phase: inspect data/template, check compute, calibrate bytes-per-token and CE/bpb target, confirm shards — establishes the problem frame before any build.

Build then explicit correctness gates BEFORE scaling: 'Smoke test param count and roundtrip' (quant/dequant load path) and 'Verify smaller ckpt size' (the <32MB budget gate) — size and roundtrip correctness locked prior to the full run.
Dedicated compute-milestone: short runs to measure step time and check compilers before committing to the full training run — sequencing capacity/compute as a checked step.

Full run launched only after gates; then 'Verify checkpoint contract and OOD probe' and 'Eval dequantized model on full val' — a post-training contract/forward done-check (notably deferred to after the first scaled run rather than fully locked before).

Improvement milestones with fallback: 'backup current ckpt' / 'Backup 0.967 ckpt, launch longer run' — preserves known-good before each targeted improvement attempt, showing frontier/fallback thinking but only along the train-longer axis.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows clearly ordered phases each with a concrete done-check — smoke-test param-count+roundtrip and size verification locked before the full run, step-time measured, baseline val_bpb established, contract/dequant verified, then improvement runs that preserve a fallback checkpoint — which exceeds the level-5 anchor's 'rough success criteria'. It falls short of a clean 8 because the full grader-interface/forward contract check was performed after the first scaled run rather than before scaling, and short of 10 because the capacity↔size↔compute tradeoff is managed only partially explicitly (mainly train-longer with a preserved backup), so I place it at 7 between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: Early 'smoke test param count and roundtrip' — verifies the int8 quantization round-trips and parameter count before committing to a run, not just relying on training loss.
'Verify smaller ckpt size with tied skip' — explicit checkpoint size verification against the 32MB budget while iterating on architecture.

'Verify checkpoint contract and OOD probe' — checks the load/forward contract and probes position-dependence of logits (the OOD probe), matching the grader's forward-signature and position requirements.
'Eval dequantized model on full val' — reloads the dequantized model independently and computes local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy against the 0.983 threshold.
'Final verification of submission checkpoint' — runs a verification gate on the actual submitted checkpoint before finishing, across multiple training runs (run2/run3).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent verifies well beyond training loss: quantization round-trip (19), size budget (25), the load/forward contract plus a position-dependence probe (158), an independent dequantized reload with full-val bpb as a calibrated proxy (160), and a final submission-checkpoint verification gate (282). This end-to-end verification through the checkpoint interface — dequant round-trip, contract/position checks, and val_bpb as a margin proxy — matches the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the descriptions don't show a single standalone harness mirroring both grader load paths with shifted-pass bpb re-run automatically as a gate on every iteration; verification appears as targeted checks rather than a unified reusable harness.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: Calibrated bytes-per-token and CE target early, establishing the val_bpb yardstick against the 0.983 threshold before training.
Repeatedly evaluated and polled val_bpb progression during the first run through warmdown to final result — active trajectory monitoring, not end-only checking.
After reading first run's result, edited the script and relaunched with a longer anneal while backing up the current checkpoint — a continue/change decision driven by the val read.
'Backup 0.967 ckpt, launch longer run' shows explicit awareness of the 0.967-vs-0.983 margin and deliberate reallocation of compute to improve margin while preserving the best checkpoint as a floor.
Tracked run3's anneal descent extensively and ran final verification, sustaining the done-vs-remaining picture across a third run.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent tracked val_bpb trajectory against the 0.983 target across three runs, calibrated compute via step-time measurements, and made continue/relaunch decisions based on the val read (longer anneal, backup-and-improve on the 0.967 checkpoint) rather than fixed step counts — matching the level-8 anchor and edging toward 9 with near-threshold margin awareness. It falls short of level 10 because there is no clear evidence of explicit plateau-vs-overfit diagnosis or recognition of diminishing returns, and the observation content is not available to confirm deeper reasoning.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: After smoke test, added tied embeddings ('tied skip') and verified the smaller checkpoint size — a targeted correction to fit the byte cap, showing size-vs-capacity awareness.
Checked for C compilers and step time, then switched to eager mode — adapting the training setup to environment/compute reality rather than repeating a failing config.
After run1's result, edited to a longer anneal schedule and relaunched, backing up the existing checkpoint first — a reasoned optimization-lever change with progress preserved.

Verified dequantized model at ~0.967 (already under target), backed it up, then launched a longer run to push lower with headroom — extending toward the threshold without risking the working solution.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent made multiple reasoned, distinct corrections tied to specific constraints — tied embeddings for the size cap, eager mode for the environment, and longer anneal/longer runs for bpb — each with the prior good checkpoint backed up so no run was a wasted sink, which is above the single-lever anchor (5). However, its primary bpb lever was repeatedly 'train/anneal longer' rather than evidence-driven trades between architecture depth/width and the quantization scheme, so it falls short of the level-8 'diagnose the binding constraint and adapt the design' bar. This places the observed behavior at 6, interpolating between the reasoned-single-lever (5) and constraint-diagnosing (8) anchors.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Calibrates bytes-per-token and a CE target before any training — sizing the goal so runs can be aimed at the threshold rather than run open-endedly.
Cheap smoke test (param count + quantization roundtrip) validates the pipeline/contract before committing compute to a long run.
Two short runs explicitly 'to measure step time' (compiled and eager) — informative probes to estimate throughput/wall-clock cost before launching the full run.
Launches full run only after probes; after run 1 finishes, edits for a longer anneal and relaunches while backing up the current checkpoint — adjusting allocation as results come in.
Verifies contract and evaluates the dequantized model, backs up the good 0.967 checkpoint, then invests in a longer run 3 — reserving a verified fallback submission (margin) before spending more.
Extended monitoring of run 3 to a final result, then final verification and cleanup — sustained, phase-structured spending across baseline, main run, and extension.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reserves cheap compute for calibration and contract smoke-tests, runs explicit short probes to measure step time before committing, sizes the main run to the goal, and then adjusts allocation across successive runs (longer anneal, longer run) as results arrive while backing up known-good checkpoints to preserve a verified submission — matching the level-8 anchor of phase-structured, self-adjusting allocation. It stops short of level 10 because the 'run longer, then longer again' pattern is empirical rather than a pre-computed estimate of the steps/capacity needed to cross 0.983, so the probes inform cost more than they inform a single right-sized investment.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
